newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan coffee prices slip but demand remains.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan coffee prices slip but demand remains.

text.p: Kenyan coffee prices slipped marginally at this week's auction following weak overseas markets but traders were optimistic there was enough demand to sustain current high prices.
On average, prices were $20 down on last week. The market average dropped to $253 Tuesday from $278 last week.
Grades ABs averaged $271 per 50-kg (110 lb) compared to $291 while grade Cs averaged $251 from $278. Grade PBs averaged $272 from $293, according to Coffee Board of Kenya (CBK) figures.
"Kenyan coffee is much sought after, especially by roasters for its unique blending quality, because it gives a fresh taste," a trader said.
Auction prices have been rising since the beginning of the year fuelled by speculative buying ahead of an anticipated shortage in producer countries.
"Prices were high, everyone tried to rush coffee into the market, which affected supply," an official from the Coffee Board of Kenya told Reuters on Wednesday.
Comparatively poorer quality coffee on offer at the auction this week did not help prices much, traders added.

"A lot of the good quality coffee was delivered early through the auction. There's more of the average and lower qualities on offer currently and these will be on offer over the next 2-3 auctions," a trader said.

They added that despite downwards pressure on the world market Kenyan prices would hold at least until end of July -- a critical period when the market was expected to seek fresh direction following new crop figures.
A shortage of washed arabicas worldwide was expected to sustain demand, traders said.
Estimates from the Coffee Board of Kenya showed some 45,000 bags had been earmarked for sale at auctions this month but that will be cut to 35,000 bags from April 9.
"This should spread the quantity to July, pending a supply review," an official said.
The CBK has revised its production forecast for 1996/97 to 78,000 tonnes from 85,000. --Wambui Chege, Nairobi Newsroom +254-2 330-261.
